name: Cola
tagline: One subscription that fronts several AI models, with a quick mode for one-liners and a deeper mode for grinding through complex coding tasks.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: A personal multi-model chat client with your own API keys is genuinely a one-session build: streaming, model switcher, conversation history in SQLite, a two-mode UI. Where it stops being a one-shot is everything that makes it a product for other people: auth, billing, usage metering, per-provider quirks around context limits, rate limits, tool calling, and the specific failure modes each API invents. The bundled-subscription angle also does not survive DIY, because you go back to paying each provider directly at token rates. If you are a heavy single user, that is often cheaper anyway. If you want the deeper iterative mode to actually feel tuned rather than just a longer prompt loop, budget a weekend and expect to keep tinkering.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app that talks to several model providers with your own keys, keeps threads in SQLite, and offers a fast one-shot mode plus an iterative refine mode that carries diffs and context forward.
requirements: API keys for at least two providers, in .env
Node 20 and a local SQLite file
Willingness to pay per token instead of a flat subscription
Patience for each provider's streaming and error format differences
whatYouLose: One bill covering multiple frontier models instead of several metered accounts
Provider failover, retry, and rate-limit handling that someone else maintains
Mobile and desktop clients with synced history
A refine mode that has been tuned against real usage, not just a loop you wrote on Sunday
Somebody else noticing when a provider silently changes an API or deprecates a model
moatNotes: The hard part is not the chat box, it is keeping six moving provider APIs from breaking in six different ways on the same afternoon.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because model aggregation is boring maintenance work that never ends. Every provider ships a new model, changes a parameter, tightens a rate limit, or invents a new streaming quirk, and a paid product absorbs that so you do not spend Tuesday debugging a 429. Add a single bill, apps on more than one device, and a refinement workflow that has been shaped by other people's complaints, and the subscription is a reasonable trade for anyone who wants to use the tool rather than own it.
notes: The chat UI is a Saturday; the ten years of provider edge cases arrive one incident at a time.
prompt:
Build a local multi-model AI chat and coding workspace. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable: Vite + React + TypeScript on the front end, Hono on Node 20 for the API, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Tailwind for styling. Single repo, one npm run dev that starts both.

Providers: read keys from .env (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY). Write one thin adapter interface with send(messages, model, opts) returning an async iterator of text chunks, then implement it once per provider against their HTTP streaming endpoints. Do not use a giant abstraction library. If a key is missing, hide that provider in the UI instead of crashing.

Data model in SQLite: threads (id, title, mode, created_at), messages (id, thread_id, role, content, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, created_at), artifacts (id, thread_id, filename, content, version).

UI, two modes only:
1. Quick: single input box, one model, streamed answer, no thread sidebar clutter. Enter sends, Cmd+Enter sends and copies the reply.
2. Deep: left sidebar of threads, main pane chat, right pane an artifact editor. In Deep mode every assistant reply may emit fenced code blocks; parse them, save each as a new artifact version, and show a diff against the previous version. A Refine button resends the current artifact plus the last user instruction so iterations build on the file, not the transcript.

Also required: model picker per message, per-thread model default, token counts and a running cost estimate using a hardcoded price table in one file, streaming cancel button, retry with exponential backoff on 429 and 5xx, export a thread to markdown.

Explicitly out of scope: auth, billing, usage limits, multi-user, hosted deploy, mobile app, RAG, vector search, agent tool execution.

Write a README with setup steps, an .env.example, and a note that costs are billed directly by each provider. Keep it runnable after npm install and one migration step.
